newsitem.title: FINLAND: M.BOTNIA TO CHECK PULP PRICES NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: M.BOTNIA TO CHECK PULP PRICES NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Finnish pulp producer Mesta-Botnia Oy Ab, owned by forest industry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy , said on Tuesday it would check its pulp prices next week.

"Early next week will decide on prices -- our policy is to follw market prices," marketing director Jyrki Yrjo-Koskinen told Reuters by telepohone, but declined to say whether Metsa-Botnia would up prices.

Metsa-Botnia last raised its prices for long-fibre pulp to $580 per tonne and for totally chlorine free (TCF) short-fibre to 460 ecu in May, but American producers have said they will hike long-fibre pulp prices by $50 to $630 per tonne on July 1.
Yrjo-Koskinen said pulp prices were on a rising trend and that May Norscan pulp stocks had developed favourably by falling to some 1.6 million tonnes.
"It is most crucial that the stocks will not rise during the summer," he said adding that their own stocks were at a favourable level.
